$comment: How the view looks from inside a fluid and at its waterline (docs/WATER_RENDERING.md §12; owner, 2026-11-07: 'a clean waterline like this', then 'the band isn't just a white line, it's supposed to be like an actual thing ... colored based on the surroundings with what looks like a darker line over a lighter line, and the underside of water has a texture'). Per fluid, by its name in the block registry (a fluid not listed takes `default`). Each pixel is under the fluid when its view ray's point on the lens plane (lensM metres ahead of the eye along the camera's forward axis) is below the fluid's surface over the eye's column, raised and lowered by the line's waves: the screen splits along a straight line, wavy by the line's waves, that moves smoothly with the eye's height. lensM: how far ahead the lens plane is (m; larger, the line sweeps the screen more slowly as the eye rises or sinks: a level view's line reaches the screen's edge with the eye lensM × tan(half the vertical FOV) from the surface, 0.3 m for 0.4 at the default FOV). line.amplitudeM, line.wavelengthM, line.speed: the line's waves on the lens plane (m, m, cycles a second; amplitude 0: a straight line; the plane spans about ±lensM × 1.2 m across the screen, so a wavelength of lensM shows a few waves). band: the surface's slab seen edge-on just under the line (the line is its top edge): depthM how deep it reaches under the line on the lens plane (m; 0: none; lensM × 1.5 m is the screen's height at the default FOV); its colour is what is around it (the scene just above the line, mirrored, over the underwater view below), times tint (sRGB multiplier, #ffffff: none); streaks the strength of its texture (the underside's cells stretched along the line, compressed toward it as a receding plane is), breakup how broken its ripples are (0: smooth parallel stripes; 1: warped, coming and going); mirror the share of it that is the scene above mirrored at most (0–1), mirrorWarpPx how far the ripples shift and blur that mirror (px of the drawing buffer; 0: a literal mirror); glints the share of bright sparkles in it; rimPx and rimShade the dark line along its top edge (px of the drawing buffer; the colour × rimShade), linePx and lineGlow the bright line just under it (px; × lineGlow). underside.texture: the strength of the light and dark cells on the surface's underside seen from below (the caustic cells on Medium and High, the noise tile on Low; 0: flat); breakup how much they read as broken bright cells with dark gaps between, some brighter than others (0: the caustic web, bright lines; 1: bright cells, dark gaps); sunPatch how much brighter they are toward the sun's image through Snell's window (0: none; its colour the sun's), sunPower how tight that patch is (the power of the cosine to it: larger, smaller); cellScale the cells' size against the floor's caustics (a whole number, 1–4: 2 halves them). The texture and the patch fade into the fog over the distance to the surface (§12.2). window: Snell's window overhead (§16), the real sky seen through it along the rays bent out by Snell's law: cells how much of the underside's cells darken and lighten that sky (0: the clear sky; 1: as on the mirror outside it), bodies how strongly the stars, the moon and the sun show in it over the sky's gradient (1: as the sky above shows them, on every tier; 0: none); the sky through it is the sky pass's own, clouds included (§16.1); sunGlow a bright blown-out glow round the sun's image in it (× the sun's light; 0: none), sunPower how tight that glow is (the power of the cosine to the sun's image: larger, smaller), rimGlow a soft bright glow round the window's rim spilling into the mirror outside it (× the sky's light straight up; 0: none). tone: the underwater colour grade (§19): fogColor the colour the fog's in-scatter is pulled toward (sRGB) by fogShare (0: the fluid's own scatter colour, as from above), brightness the in-scatter's brightness (×; 1: as lit), mirror the surface's mirror outside the window (total internal reflection) brighter by (×), floorLight the share of the fluid's absorption the light reaching the floor and what is under the surface takes (1: all of it; lower, the floor keeps more of its colour). fog: the fluid's absorption and scattering (the block registry's fluid look) over the distance in the fluid, but only past clearM metres (0: from the eye) and scaled by density (1: the registry's own rates, as from above; lower reads clearer and farther, higher murkier). Run `node shared/look/underwater.mjs` after editing; CI fails if crates/dwell-look/src/underwater.gen.rs is stale. The content is prototype (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1).
